## Summary

Fix the observed GitHub Pages deployment race and standardize the public Tribute navigation.

### Evidence / root cause
The 2026-11-01 Pages run `41290649940` built successfully, then failed during `deploy-pages` with HTTP 400 because another Pages deployment was still in progress. The source publisher was writing `/help-wanted/` and `/matrix/` to the same external `main` branch in two separate pushes per run, creating avoidable overlapping Pages deployments.

### Changes
- Publish Tribute and Matrix into one combined artifact and one external-repository commit per run.
- Publish the canonical public route at `/tribute/`; keep `/help-wanted/` populated as a compatibility alias so existing links do not break.
- Centralize primary navigation in `site-nav.js`; the shared `versioning.js` module loads it for dashboard pages, and Matrix/project-hub builds copy the same module.
- Ensure preview publishing uses `/previews/<key>/tribute/`, shares the production publication lock, and republishes the current production snapshot plus the preview in one atomic external commit; preview sitemap/robots metadata stays scoped to the preview route.
- Update page identity, sitemap/robots references, navigation labels and deployment documentation to use Tribute.
- Extend the dashboard verification script to assert that the shared navigation module and canonical destinations exist.

### Validation
- Inspected actual Actions job logs for run `41290649940`: build success, deploy failure due to an in-progress deployment.
- Static source-level checks are added to the existing dashboard verifier; CI should execute them on this PR.
- Production publication and browser-level URL verification remain pending until the PR is merged and the publisher runs.

## Added
- `.github/workflows/apk-xref-exec.yml` — workflow_dispatch per request issue (input: issue_number). Ephemeral runner isolation; permissions {} top, job contents:read + issues:write; no provisioned secrets. Steps: fetch filing (refuses without the apk-xref label) → run the belt → file findings issue → post intake record → report verdict + findings link on the request issue → upload findings-only evidence artifact (90d).
- `ops/web_adapter_foundry/apk_xref_exec.py` — the runner: parses the filing's form headings, drives apk_xref.py (acquire [exit 3 = no-artifact evidence outcome] → extract [provenance injected] → git clone target repo → scan-repo → xref; or the no-artifact record), emits the belt's own findings markdown (apk-xref/v1 seam, PR #2143) + run summary. File-in/file-out — issue filing stays in the workflow shell (gh).
- `tests/test_apk_xref_exec.py` — filing→spec seam, 4/4. Offline end-to-end smoke (none-known source): verdict no-artifact-found, findings in form headings verbatim.

## Platform subtlety, handled
Issues created with a workflow GITHUB_TOKEN do not retrigger other workflows, so a token-filed findings issue can never wake apk-xref-intake. The exec workflow runs the same deterministic intake parser itself and posts the record carrying the intake workflow's own hash-dedupe marker; a later human edit re-runs intake, which skips its duplicate. Disclosed on the record comment itself.

## Not in this PR
Mass dispatch of the 31 filings — dispatch is per-issue by design (concurrency group per issue); the Foundry lane dispatches the wave, or a batch dispatch list can follow.
